# Model overview

This open R simulation by Wood and colleagues examines hypothetical intensive-care triage strategies when COVID-19 demand might exceed capacity. It compares first-come, first-served admission, triage when demand is expressed and reverse triage. Inputs include demand, length of stay, capacity and assumptions about patient outcomes; outputs include lives and life-years lost. The model has been independently reproduced through the STARS project.

## Actions for participants before the session

- Attempt to reproduce the model by using GitHub Codespaces (recommended for participants new to GitHub) or by cloning the [original model repository](https://github.com/nhs-bnssg-analytics/triage-modelling) and running it locally.
- Run one of the supplied R analysis scripts and inspect the resulting output.
- Explore the repository and its structure.

::: {.callout-warning title="Local software requirement"}
**This model uses R.** To run it locally, you will need R installed and will need to install the packages required by the repository. Older analytical environments may require specific package versions.

Tested setup instructions will be added here before the session.
:::

## Getting help

If you have a problem running or reusing the intensive-care triage simulation, the model's issue tracker will be the best way to contact the ReModel team. **Issue tracker link: [to be added].** When reporting a problem, describe what you were trying to do, what happened and any error messages you received.

## Session objectives and outline

This will be a discussion session around the model and our attempts to run the model as it currently exists. Participants will discuss:

- any issues they had in running the model in its current form;
- any areas of the model they didn't understand;
- how we think the model is structured from inputs through to outputs;
- how patient groups, ICU admission, capacity constraints and triage decisions are represented;
- assumptions for demand, length of stay, capacity and patient outcomes;
- where they think this model might be useful.

The aim is for participants to leave this session with a clear understanding of how to run the model and a working version of the model that they can continue to explore before the Reuse session.
